# The web client is an SDK generated by Hey API, not openapi-fetch over generated types

The codegen research (`docs/research/codegen-toolchain.md`) picked `openapi-typescript` + `openapi-fetch` for
`web/` because `@hey-api/openapi-ts` declares `engines.node >= 22.18` and the local Node was 22.11. In practice the
frontend then called `fetch` by hand against the generated types, and the Hexlet review required the frontend to go
through a generated client SDK. We switched `web/` to `@hey-api/openapi-ts` (fetch client, `baseUrl: "/api"`), which
emits one typed function per operationId into `web/src/generated/api/` as part of `make generate`; `web/src/api.ts`
only maps the SDK's error responses to typed errors. The server keeps `openapi-typescript` types plus
`fastify-openapi-glue`.

## Consequences

- `make generate` needs Node ≥ 22.18 locally (nvm Node 22.23.3); CI and Docker already run a fresh Node 22. Running
  the app, tests and builds still works on Node ≥ 22.13 — the SDK is plain TypeScript with no Node floor at runtime.
- The generator is pinned to an exact version: its output is committed and checked for drift in CI.
- The SDK calls `fetch(Request)` with `baseUrl + path`; under jsdom that needs an absolute base, so web tests set
  `client.setConfig({ baseUrl: \`${origin}/api\` })` in `web/test/setup.ts`.
